record.original_question: Determine for which permutations σ and π the order complex Δ(σ, π) associated with the interval [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset is shellable.

evidence.quote: 4. For which σ and π is ∆(σ, π) shellable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ denote the set of all finite permutations, where a permutation of length $n$ is a sequence $\pi = \pi_1\pi_2\cdots\pi_n$ in which each of $1,2,\ldots,n$ appears exactly once. For permutations $\sigma$ of length $k$ and $\pi$ of length $n$, say that $\pi$ contains $\sigma$ as a pattern, written $\sigma \le \pi$, if there exist indices $1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \le n$ such that the subsequence $\pi_{i_1}\pi_{i_2}\cdots\pi_{i_k}$ has the same relative order as $\sigma_1\sigma_2\cdots\sigma_k$ (i.e., $\pi_{i_a} < \pi_{i_b}$ if and only if $\sigma_a < \sigma_b$). This relation makes $S$ into a poset, the permutation pattern poset.

For $\sigma \le \pi$ in $S$, let $[\sigma,\pi] = \{\tau \in S : \sigma \le \tau \le \pi\}$ be the closed interval, and let $\Delta(\sigma,\pi)$ denote the order complex of the open interval $(\sigma,\pi)$, i.e., the abstract simplicial complex whose faces are the chains $\sigma < \tau_1 < \tau_2 < \cdots < \tau_r < \pi$ in $S$.

Recall that a pure or non-pure simplicial complex is shellable if its facets can be ordered $F_1, F_2, \ldots, F_t$ so that for each $i \ge 2$ and each $j < i$, there exist some $\ell < i$ and some vertex $v \in F_i \setminus F_\ell$ with $F_i \cap F_j \subseteq F_i \cap F_\ell$ and $F_i \setminus F_\ell = \{v\}$.

Problem: Characterize all pairs $(\sigma,\pi)$ with $\sigma \le \pi$ in the permutation pattern poset for which the order complex $\Delta(\sigma,\pi)$ is shellable.
artifact.status_search_result: A complete characterization of pairs $(\sigma,\pi)$ for which $\Delta(\sigma,\pi)$ is shellable appears to remain open. Partial results exist: McNamara and Steingrímsson (2015) showed that "almost all" intervals are not shellable due to non-trivial disconnected subintervals, and they characterized shellability for intervals of layered permutations (where absence of non-trivial disconnected subintervals is equivalent to shellability), conjecturing the same for separable permutations. Sagan and Willenbring proved intervals of permutations with a fixed number of descents are shellable. No general characterization has been published.

status_evidence.title: On the topology of the permutation pattern poset
status_evidence.snippet: Almost all intervals in the permutation pattern poset have non-trivial disconnected subintervals and are thus not shellable. For layered permutations, having no disconnected subintervals is equivalent to shellability; conjectured the same for separable permutations.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results characterize shellability in restricted cases; the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Intervals of permutations with a fixed number of descents are shellable
status_evidence.snippet: Intervals of permutations with a fixed number of descents are shown to be shellable.
status_evidence.claim: A specific family of intervals is known to be shellable, but no full classification is given.
